supporting_observations.claim: At 13:50:21 UTC, WS-JFROST-01 sent 51,000,494 bytes to the internal explicit proxy at 10.53.20.30:8080; the connection lasted about 13.5 seconds and received 8,985 bytes. This supports a large workstation-to-proxy transfer, but does not establish the ultimate Internet destination.
GoogleDriveFS.exe was launched on WS-JFROST-01 under julia.frost at 13:22:08 UTC. The available records do not link that process to the large transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor status reports a collection outage from 13:25 to 14:20 UTC for WS-JFROST-01 winsec and sysmon logs and for proxy logs. This covers the alert window and the large flow at 13:50.

Zeek connection telemetry is available for the large flow, but the supplied record identifies only the workstation-to-proxy connection and byte counts, not its external destination, application, or content.
claims_not_established: Whether the 13:50:21 flow is the same activity as the alert described as occurring around 13:46 UTC.
The external host or service receiving the data beyond the proxy.
Which process initiated the flow, what data was transferred, or whether the transfer was authorized or malicious.

additional_evidence_needed: Recover proxy logs for the window, including CONNECT destination, tunnel byte counts, and any available user or URL details.
Recover WS-JFROST-01 endpoint process and network telemetry for the window to attribute the flow to a process.
Review relevant Google Drive and Microsoft 365/OneDrive audit or sync records, plus file-access or DLP records, to identify the destination and data involved.
unrelated_findings: GoogleDriveFS.exe was running on WS-JFROST-01, while the supplied inventory approves Microsoft 365/OneDrive but no other cloud-storage service. Track this as a separate policy/compliance finding; the available evidence does not connect it to the alerted transfer. Supporting records: T159-00011, T159-00013.
